title: Zimmermann Telegram Excerpt — 1917

notes: This is the famous telegram from German Foreign Secretary Arthur Zimmermann to the German Minister in Mexico, proposing a German-Mexican alliance. The code numbers represent entries in German diplomatic codebook 13040. Room 40's decryption brought the United States into WWI.

source_provenance.archive: UK National Archives; Barbara Tuchman 'The Zimmermann Telegram' (1958)

historical_context: Decoded by Room 40 in January 1917, the Zimmermann Telegram proposed that Mexico attack the United States in exchange for Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona. Its revelation accelerated US entry into WWI.
known_solution_method: Partial codebook reconstruction from earlier intercepts; Nigel de Grey and William Montgomery exploited overlapping code groups.

historical_context: The Culper Spy Ring (1778–1783) was Washington's most successful intelligence network. Tallmadge (known as John Bolton, code 721) designed a numerical codebook and invisible-ink system. The ring uncovered Benedict Arnold's treason and the planned British seizure of West Point.
known_solution_method: Tallmadge codebook: numbers 1–763 map to common English words; numbers above 763 map to letters and proper names.

title: Navajo Code Talkers — WWII Pacific Transmission
ciphertext: WOL-LA-CHEE YEH-HES AH-JAH AH-NAH-HO DIBEH-YAZZIE BE LIN AH-JAH NAH-AS-TSOSI GLOE-IH TSE-NILL
source: USMC Navajo Code Talker Dictionary, declassified 1968. Documented in Doris Paul, 'The Navajo Code Talkers' (1973); Philip Johnston's 1942 proposal to the USMC.
notes: The Navajo Code Talkers used a two-level system: common military terms had specific Navajo words (e.g., 'turtle' = tank), while other words were spelled out using Navajo words for each letter (multiple Navajo words per letter for homophony). Never broken by Japan.

source_provenance.archive: USMC Navajo Code Dictionary (declassified 1968); Doris Paul (1973)

historical_context: 420 Navajo Code Talkers served in the USMC 1942–1945. Their code was the only military code in WWII never broken by the enemy. Major Howard Connor, USMC, stated: 'Were it not for the Navajos, the Marines would never have taken Iwo Jima.'

title: Polybius Square — Greek Military Signaling Example
source: Polybius, 'Histories' Book X, Chapter 44 (c. 150 BCE). The signaling system described by Polybius used torches to communicate the row and column of each letter.
notes: Polybius described a fire-signaling system where two groups of torches indicated the row and column of a letter in a 5×5 grid. Each letter required two signal bursts — one for the row (1–5), one for the column (1–5).
historical_context: Polybius (~200–118 BCE) described this fire-signaling system in his Histories as a practical military communication method. The same grid was later adapted by Trithemius and others as a secret writing system.
known_solution_method: Standard 5×5 grid with ABCDEFGHIKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ (I=J). Each number pair (row, column) maps directly to a letter.

title: Babington Plot Cipher — Mary Queen of Scots, 1586
plaintext: PROCEED WITH THE PLAN SIX GENTLEMEN ARE READY TO ACT
source: Babington Plot, 1586. Cipher attributed to Gilbert Gifford; deciphered by Thomas Phelippes for Sir Francis Walsingham. Documented in Calendar of State Papers, Scotland, Vol. VIII.
notes: The Babington Plot cipher used a nomenclator combining a 23-letter substitute alphabet with code symbols for common words and double-letter indicators. Thomas Phelippes decoded the conspirators' letters, providing evidence for Mary's execution.

source_provenance.archive: Calendar of State Papers Scotland Vol VIII; David Kahn 'The Codebreakers' (1967)

historical_context: The Babington Plot (1586) was a Catholic conspiracy to assassinate Queen Elizabeth I and place Mary Queen of Scots on the throne. Walsingham's cryptanalyst Thomas Phelippes decoded the correspondence, allowing Walsingham to identify all conspirators. Mary was executed February 8, 1587.
known_solution_method: Frequency analysis of nomenclator symbols; recovery of high-frequency code groups. Phelippes forged a postscript requesting conspirators' names.
